newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor reducing car production.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor reducing car production.

text.p: South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co has reduced production at some vehicle assembly lines by four hours a day, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
Spokesman Min Kyung-hwan said Hyundai Motor, a unit of the Hyundai Group, cut production of its once-best selling Sonata, Marcia and Avante by a combined 300 units a day from Monday.
"Line workers for those cars will not work overtime. The production curtailment will continue probably until September when we will introduce a new model of mini-van," Min said.
Assembly lines for luxury cars -- the Grandeur and Dynasty models -- will operate normally, he said.
Hyundai Motor normally runs assembly lines for 20 hours in two shifts a day, including four hours of regular overtime.
"This decision aims to reduce our rising inventory, as our domestic sales have been sluggish due to a slowdown in the economy," Min said.
Hyundai Motor has also been hurt by competition from Daewoo models, including Korea's best-selling car in March, the sub-compact Nubira.
Hyundai's domestic vehicle sales fell 16.2 percent year-on-year to 50,382 units in March.
Hyundai Motor temporarily reduced vehicle production last week by four hours for five days to reduce inventory.
Its inventory shot up to 80,000 vehicles as of Monday from 54,000 last Tuesday, when the company began the temporary production cut.
